edges.description: Generalized neuronal sphingolipid storage together with loss of neurotrophic intact prosaposin causes severe cortical neuronal loss.
Central nervous system multi-sphingolipid storage provokes reactive fibrillary astrocytosis and elevated proinflammatory cytokine expression.
Oligodendroglial and myelin-sheath sphingolipid catabolic failure impairs myelin maintenance and drives active white-matter demyelination.
Reticuloendothelial macrophage engorgement with undegraded sphingolipids drives visceral storage infiltration of the liver and spleen.
Massive cortical neuronal depopulation and loss of neurotrophic intact prosaposin manifest clinically as fulminant neonatal neurodegeneration.
Severe cortical neuronal storage and loss precipitate neonatal myoclonic and generalized seizures.
Elevated CNS proinflammatory cytokine signaling precedes and exacerbates progressive white-matter myelin loss.
Active white-matter myelin breakdown and axonal loss manifest as CNS demyelination.
Histiocytic sphingolipid storage infiltration of the liver and spleen produces neonatal hepatosplenomegaly.
Visceral reticuloendothelial storage and hepatosplenomegaly are accompanied by neonatal thrombocytopenia, although the intervening hematologic mechanism is not directly established in case reports.

nodes.description: Biallelic null PSAP variants abolish the prosaposin precursor, eliminating all four saposins (A-D). Each saposin is an essential cofactor for a distinct lysosomal sphingolipid hydrolase, so their combined loss simultaneously impairs multiple degradation pathways.
